main_body: A hide or canvas panel with a teal pattern, stretched inside a wooden frame with a lower beam and short legs, drawn face-on
top_band: none on the main body. The top beam at rows 1-3 is a thin dark-brown rim. Only the bottom beam has a lighter brown band (rows 17-19, about 2-3px), and that is a small detail.
evidence: A column through the middle goes from a dark-brown top rim (rows 1-3) straight into the yellow hide panel (rows 4-16). That panel is a vertical face with a pattern painted flat on it. There is no top band, front-edge line or eave shadow on the upper beam, and the panel is not inset into the frame. The lower beam shows a thin lighter band above a darker front, but it is too small to count as a visible top surface for the main body. The beams and posts are flat elevation strips, so this reads as a front elevation.

style.evidence: The hide has a few yellow tones with teal pattern dashes and some dark spots, so it is not a flat fill. The wood frame has only about 3 steps and is simple next to the roofed well and stall. The outline is a dark brown that leans near-black in places, with darker pixels at the frame edges. Overall it is thinner and less richly shaded than the references, with fewer steps per material and lower tile density.
